claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The fcc/B2 lamellae form continuous phase interfaces.
The as-cast alloy has high room-temperature strength.
The as-cast alloy has limited ductility because of catastrophic interfacial cracking under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Thermomechanical treatment can tune the mechanical properties of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Severe plastic deformation at elevated temperature followed by controlled cooling will transform the lamellar microstructure into a patterned, discontinuous, or equiaxed configuration.
A treatment temperature of 600–800°C corresponds to approximately 0.6–0.7 Tm for this alloy.
The 600–800°C window will permit dynamic recrystallization while avoiding excessive grain growth or phase decomposition.
Pressure above 1 GPa is required to induce the proposed severe plastic deformation.
A strain rate of 10^-1 to 10^0 s^-1 is suitable for the proposed treatment.
Controlled cooling will stabilize the patterned or equiaxed microstructure.
The treatment will induce dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement that break up continuous fcc/B2 interfaces.
The transformed structure will contain high-angle grain boundaries.
High-angle grain boundaries and discontinuous interfaces will impede crack propagation.
Breaking continuous interfaces will reduce stress concentrations at phase boundaries.
The transformed microstructure will promote homogeneous dislocation distribution, dislocation storage, strain hardening, and uniform plasticity.
The treatment will produce room-temperature tensile elongation above 20% while maintaining or increasing strength.
The treatment will reduce catastrophic interfacial cracking and yield more uniform deformation during uniaxial tension.
Conventional HIP at 1400°C and 200 MPa for 2 hours will not induce the same severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization as HITMT.
If HIP leaves the lamellae intact and fails to improve ductility relative to HITMT, that result would falsify the claim that HITMT is necessary.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes the as-cast lamellar alloy as having low ductility and a strength–ductility trade-off, whereas the cited same-system records explicitly characterize that as-cast lamellar alloy as having an unusually favorable balance of high strength and high ductility.

Failure of the lower-pressure HIP control to reproduce HITMT's microstructure or ductility would support, rather than falsify, the proposition that severe deformation or extreme pressure is necessary. The stated falsification logic is directionally reversed.
